newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian shares end lower, no foreign buying seen.
newsitem.headline: Colombian shares end lower, no foreign buying seen.

text.p: Colombian shares ended mostly lower for the third consecutive session as a dearth of foreign fund buying continued to weigh on the market, brokers said.
"Local investors are dominating the market and they always tend to sell after periodic gains," one Medellin-based broker said in a telephone interview.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index shed 0.37 percent to end at 18,354.71. Bogota's IBB index closed down 0.32 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,209.90.
Leading losers included brewer Bavaria, the country's single biggest private company.

It gave up 0.62 percent in Bogota and Medellin, ending at 7,948 and 7,950 pesos per share, respectively, on what brokers described as a strong bout of profit-taking after its sharp run- up earlier this year.
Banco de Bogota, Colombia's third largest bank in terms of the assets, fell 0.74 percent in Bogota, meanwhile, ending at 6,650 pesos per share.
Blue-chip Banco Ganadero continued to defy the market's downward trend, however. It closed up 0.49 percent in Bogota at an all-time high of 410 pesos per share.
